  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "kind": "bustout",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "The chargeback breach warrants investigation, but negative volume_z and ticket_drift below 1 do not support a sales ramp. Fulfillment failures, thin buyer accounts and settlement extraction are unverified."
    },
    {
      "kind": "marketing_push",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "A legitimate campaign could explain changes in buyer mix or dispute composition, but no campaign evidence is supplied and the metrics do not show elevated volume."
    },
    {
      "kind": "data_issue",
      "likelihood": "low",
      "reasoning": "Missing orders or duplicated dispute records could distort the rate, but no pipeline defect is observed. Reconciliation would test this possibility cheaply."
    }
  ],
  "recommended_action": "monitor",
  "evidence_gaps": [
    "Inspect the three dispute records for reason, status, underlying order and duplication; reconcile the 105-order denominator against source records.",
    "Check promised delivery dates, tracking and delivery confirmation for disputed orders and a small recent-order sample; inspect unresolved fulfillment complaints.",
    "Reconcile refund requests, approvals and processor records to determine whether zero recorded refunds reflects actual activity or missing processing/data.",
    "Check campaign and promotion dates against sales and disputed orders; compare relevant category patterns.",
    "If fulfillment failures emerge, inspect associated buyer-account history and settlement records for coordinated purchases and payout extraction."
  ],
  "memo_markdown": "Merchant 31 triggered a chargeback breach: 3 disputes across 105 trailing-30-day orders (2.9%). GMV was 951117 cents. Volume_z is -1.40 and ticket_drift is 0.895, so the observed pattern does not support a sales ramp. Recorded refunds are zero; that does not establish successful fulfillment.\n\nRecommend monitor, with prompt review of the three disputes and a small fulfillment sample. Current evidence establishes a dispute-rate breach, not corroborated bust-out behavior.\n\nConfirm concern through overdue or undelivered orders, consistent non-delivery disputes, and linked evidence of coordinated thin-account purchases and settlement extraction. Verified fulfillment, legitimate dispute explanations and reconciled order/refund records would weaken the bust-out hypothesis. Campaign records could support a benign explanation; missing orders or duplicate disputes could explain the alert through a data issue.\n\nA human should reassess payout controls if these checks reveal broader non-delivery or coordinated extraction."
}
